prerequisites: basic mathematics topics: algebra, elementary geometry, logarithms, trigonometry, basic elemental differential and integral calculus, first and second degree equations and inequalities, algebraic systems

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with a complete picture of the basic elements of classical mechanics with particular reference to those topics closely related to engineering.
Provide knowledge of the basic concepts of classical mechanics in a concise and correct way for the applications.
Enable the student to master the theoretical knowledge acquired and to be able to solve exercises related to classical mechanics problems.

Provide the student with the ability to explain the knowledge acquired in a clear and rigorous way. The student must be able to correctly state definitions, problems and theorems relating to the contents of the course.

Motivate students to learn critically and responsibly all the topics exposed during lessons in the classroom and to enrich their judgment capacities through the study of the educational materials indicated by the teacher.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO PHYSICS. PHYSICAL QUANTITIES, DIMENSIONS AND UNIT OF MEASURE. PHYSICAL MEASUREMENTS AND MEASUREMENT ERRORS
MATERIAL POINT KINEMATICS, STUDY OF MOTIONS IN ONE, TWO AND MORE THAN TWO DIMENSIONS
MATERIAL POINT DYNAMICS. FORCES. NEWTON'S FIRST AND SECOND LAW. INERTIAL MASS AND GRAVITATIONAL MASS. REFERENCE SYSTEMS
MATERIAL POINT DYNAMICS. NEWTON'S THIRD LAW. CONSTRAINTS AND BOUNDARY REACTIONS. FRICTIONS. FORCES: GRAVITY, ELASTICITY
CENTRAL FORCES, CENTRIPETAL FORCES. FRICTION AND VISCOUS FORCES. REFERENCE SYSTEMS IN RELATIVE MOTION
THEOREM OF KINETIC ENERGY. KINETIC ENERGY
WORK DONE BY GRAVITATIONAL ENERGY, WORK DONE BY KINETIC ENERGY, WORK DONE BY A GENERIC VARIABLE FORCE, POWER
POTENTIAL ENERGY AND CONSERVATIVE SYSTEMS. WORK DONE BY AN EXTERNAL FORCE. CONSERVATION OF ENERGY

DYNAMICS OF MATERIAL POINT SYSTEMS. INNER FORCES IN MULTIPLE POINT SYSTEMS. DENSITY. CENTER OF MASS: DISCRETE AND CONTINUOUS CASE. THEOREMS ON THE CENTER OF MASS. KINETIC ENERGY OF A MATERIAL POINT SYSTEM AND THE KOENIG THEOREM. MOMENTUM, CONSERVATION OF MOMENTUM
SCATTERING PROCESSES IN ONE AND TWO DIMENSIONS.
THE CARDINAL EQUATIONS OF DYNAMICS FOR MULTIPLE POINT SYSTEMS. ANGULAR MOMENTUM, CONSERVATION OF ANGULAR MOMENTUM
FUNDAMENTAL ELEMENTS OF DYNAMICS AND STATICS OF RIGID BODIES.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and an oral test. The written test involves solving three problems, each scored from 0 to 10, for a total of 0 to 30. A minimum score of 18 on the written test is required to proceed to the oral test. The oral test consists of three questions, each scored from 0 to 10, for a total of 0 to 30. The final grade is the average of the written and oral test scores. Midterm tests may be administered, granting direct access to the oral exam if successful.
